Issue Summary: LTA Result Cron - System patched NPS as ENA instead of RD1 for Diplomat Notices after processing
Description: Issue 1: LTA result cron patched the Next Procssing Stage to ENA instead of RD1 for Diplomat notices. Root cause: LTA Download uses an in-memory cache (LtaCachingTableQueryProxy) to reduce repeated database reads during batch processing. The cache works like this: 1. Before batch runs → cache is pre-loaded with all notices that will be processed. 2. On every write (patch / post) → the cache entry for that notice is removed, so the next read does not return stale data. 3. On every read (query) → the cache is checked first. The bug is in step 3: when the cache entry had already been removed in step 2, the read logic returned an empty list instead of falling back to the real database. The caller then treated "empty" as "this notice does not exist" and skipped the next update. Why only Diplomat: - The Diplomat code path is the only one that calls cachedPatch on ocms_valid_offence_notice (to set vehicle_registration_type = 'D'). - That write invalidated the VON cache entry for the notice. - The very next step (updateProcessingStageToRD1) read the same cache → got empty → skipped the RD1 update. - Standard / VIP never trigger that patch, so their VON cache entry stayed intact and the RD1 update succeeded. Why not caught in Round 1–3 of OCMS-SR-2026-003: - Round 1 and 2 addressed different bugs (field mappings, error reporting, road tax date). - Round 3 fixed a related cache problem on the write side (duplicate-key INSERT converted to UPDATE). - This new bug is on the read side — on

Description: Reported By Sharleen Tan - 19 June 2026 Tier Admin Private API (ocmsadminprivateapi) Background info The MHA NRIC download cron processes batch response files containing address verification results. For each UIN (offender ID) in the response, the code updates two things: (1) the owner/driver record (ONOD) and (2) the MHA registration address. However, the address update iterates over ALL notices linked to that UIN, regardless of which batch triggered the enquiry. Problem Description When Batch 1 ran at 6:16pm, it overwrote the address records of 15 Batch 2 notices that had already been correctly updated at 10:30am. The address update at MhaNricDownloadHelper.java:734-747 uses onodByUin (keyed by uin only) to iterate ALL notices for the same ID, while the ONOD update at line 782 uses onodKey (keyed by uin|idType|noticeNo) scoped to the specific batch notice. The noticeNoRef (uraReferenceNo) from the MHA response is available at line 700 but is not used to filter the address update loop. Impact Address records for notices processed in earlier batches are overwritten when a later batch processes the same offender ID. This affects any offender with notices across multiple batches. Batch 2 notices that were correctly updated at 10:30am had their addresses overwritten by Batch 1 at 6:16pm — confirmed for 15 notices. Workaround No workaround — affected address records must be manually corrected
